battery.capacity_gross_kwh.notes: InsideEVs: 'US FWD: 71.4 kWh, rated up to 150 kW'. EV Pulse also lists 71.4 kWh for the front-drive bZ4X.

battery.capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 64.0 kWh usable for the 71.4 kWh bZ4X pack (European listing, MY22-24); the US/Canada FWD uses the same 71.4 kWh pack (InsideEVs). Bjorn Nyland measured 57.7-60.8 kWh on a European 71.4 kWh car, so the true figure may be lower.

battery.chemistry.notes: Autopian (chief engineer): 'The bZ4X used two different nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) battery packs depending on the motor configuration'. EV Database also lists NMC for the 71.4 pack.

battery.nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 355 V nominal for the 71.4 kWh pack, the 400 V class; Toyota's chief engineer says the bZ 'still runs on a 400-volt electrical architecture' (InsideEVs).

battery.preconditioning.notes: Estimated: 2023-25 bZ4X (US and Canada). EV Database lists battery preconditioning as "No" for the 2022-24 bZ4X; Toyota's 2026 pages present battery preconditioning as a feature standard on the 2026 bZ (Toyota USA 2026 release; InsideEVs calls it new), and Toyota Canada says it exists on 'select models only'. No page for the 2023-25 cars describes a battery preconditioning control, so none is recorded. Weakest for 2025 (the 2025 European update added it; North America unconfirmed).

dc_max_kw.notes: InsideEVs: FWD 71.4 kWh 'rated up to 150 kW'. EV Pulse: the AWD rate was raised to 150 kW 'matching the front-drive model'. Toyota Canada FAQ: 10-80% 'in as quickly as 28 minutes' with a 150 kW or higher charger. Same across 2023-2025.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: InsideEVs/Out of Spec describes the US Limited AWD with a 6.6 kW on-board charger; EV Database lists 6.6 kW standard for the 2022-24 bZ4X; Toyota's 2026 release says the new 11 kW charger is 'up from 7 kW on the prior model'. Carried over to all 2023-25 bZ4X (EV Pulse quotes 7.6 kW, probably a typo).

charge_port.notes: Toyota Canada release footnote: "MY2023-25 BEV drivers will need an CCS1 to J3400 adapter" to use NACS plugs, so the car's own port is CCS1. The US page says the same (CCS to J3400 adapter).
Toyota USA release footnote: "MY2023-25 BEV drivers will need a CCS to J3400 adapter (aka NACS Adapter)"; the 2026 bZ is the first with a standard NACS inlet.

supercharger_access.notes: Toyota USA: 2023-25 bZ4X owners need a CCS to J3400 adapter and get one free through a dealer from November 2025 (current state).
Toyota Canada: the NACS adaptor is designed exclusively for 2025 and earlier Toyota BEV models; with it owners can use the NACS network. Drive Tesla Canada reports the free adapter for 2023-25 bZ4X.

charge_port.notes: Estimated: EV Specifications lists CCS1 for the North American 2023-25 Solterra; Subaru (Oct 2025) says 2023-2025 owners need a NACS adapter and only the 2026 has a NACS port; Toyota says its 2023-25 twin has a CCS1 port.

supercharger_access.notes: Subaru of America (22 Oct 2025): owners of 2023-2025 Solterra can purchase a Genuine Subaru Accessory Fast Charging Adapter (NACS); all Solterra owners have access to 25,000+ Tesla Superchargers.
Drive Tesla Canada: Subaru says all Solterra EV owners can access 25,000+ Superchargers in Canada and the US; 2023-2025 owners will buy the NACS adapter from Subaru dealers.
